extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for academic journals (PLOS audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for academic peer reviewers on how to read a submitted manuscript, what to evaluate, and how to structure the review to help editors decide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether authors' claims are supported
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the authors' claims are supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary reviewer job: focus on whether the data, analyses, and arguments in the paper actually back the stated claims; examine methods, results, figures, and data to confirm support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help the journal editors make their decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Help the journal editors make their decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary reviewer job: provide an assessment and recommendation that helps editors weigh the manuscript's strengths, weaknesses, and suitability for the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the research question
rubrics_metrics.description: What research question is being addressed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the manuscript clearly states a focused, answerable research question and that the question is important and relevant to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the methodology used
rubrics_metrics.description: What methodology did the authors use?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the chosen design and methods are appropriate for answering the research question and are described with sufficient detail to evaluate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate the work to existing literature
rubrics_metrics.description: How does this relate to existing literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the manuscript situates the work within prior studies, accurately represents the literature, and clarifies the incremental contribution or novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify main findings and supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the main findings and supporting evidence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract the central results and check that the evidence presented (data, analyses, figures) legitimately supports the stated findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended reading order
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested sequence for reading a manuscript: 1. Abstract and introduction. 2. Figures and tables with results. 3. Conclusions. 4. Complete manuscript from start to finish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this order to get a top-line view of the study and its evidence before reading the whole text; helps identify major strengths/weaknesses quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract and Introduction — significance and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it explain why the study matters? Are connections to existing research clear?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the abstract/introduction justify the study's importance, define the question/hypothesis, and clearly link to prior work and gaps the study addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and Tables — clarity and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Are they clear and readable? Do captions accurately describe content? Are axes labeled correctly? Do they genuinely support the findings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine visual data presentation for readability, correct labeling, accurate captions, and direct relevance to the paper's claims; ensure figures/tables are not misleading or ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — technical soundness and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the research technically sound? Are controls and conditions adequate? Is there sufficient data for conclusions? Are limitations addressed? Could another researcher reproduce this?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess methodological rigor, appropriateness of controls/conditions, sample size/data sufficiency, transparency of procedures, and whether methods are described in enough detail for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results and Discussion — support and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do results actually support conclusions? Do conclusions overstate findings? Are study limitations discussed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check alignment between results and authors' interpretations; flag overreach or unsupported claims; ensure authors acknowledge limitations and alternative explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is methodology appropriate? (Note if you lack expertise.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether statistical methods are suitable, correctly applied, and reported; explicitly state if you cannot assess statistical validity due to limited expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and supporting information — sufficiency and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Is evidence sufficient for claims? Can others recreate the analyses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify availability and completeness of data, code, and supplementary materials needed to reproduce analyses; note if evidence is insufficient to support conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to ignore / reviewer conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual typos or minor writing errors (mention only that the paper needs language editing). Don't use references to promote your own work. Focus on substance over writing quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize substantive scientific assessment over minor language issues; note language-editing needs but avoid overemphasis on copyediting; do not use the review to self-promote via citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: "Everything you have access to as a reviewer needs to stay confidential until the work is published."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain strict confidentiality about manuscript content and reviewer comments until publication; do not share or publicize unpublished results or use them for personal advantage.
